title: B2B Appointment Setting Cold Call Script
seoTitle: B2B Appointment Setting Cold Call Script
secondaryKeywords: cold calling script to book a meeting
subindustry: A parts supplier calling a distributor
serviceCategory: Booking a qualified first sales meeting
objective: Book a first meeting around one problem the buyer wants to solve
icp: Use the blank version for your own offer. The worked call is for a parts supplier reaching a distributor.
scenario: A rep wants a first meeting with the person who buys replacement parts for a distributor.
metaDescription: Use this B2B appointment setting cold call script to qualify a buyer, handle “send me an email” and book a first meeting. Copy the template and worked example.
opening: Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Supplier]. We help distributors find parts when their usual supplier is out. Do you look after purchasing for the branch?
quickAnswer: A B2B appointment setter needs three answers before booking. Does this person own the issue? What happens when it comes up? What would the buyer want to do in a meeting? Use their answer in the invitation.
questions: When a customer needs a part you don’t have, how do you find it today?
When you can’t find it in time, what happens to the order?
Is there one part you’ve had trouble finding more than once?
bridge: Got it. That’s why I called. We can check other sources for [part they named].
cta: Would you be open to ten minutes with our parts specialist to look at that one together?
fullScript:
[Open. Use an offer your team can deliver.]
Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Supplier]. We help distributors find parts when their usual supplier is out. Do you look after purchasing for the branch?

[If yes, pause after each question.]
Curious to ask, when a customer needs a part you don’t have, how do you find it today?

[Buyer: “We already have two suppliers.”]
Makes sense. When they’re both out, can the branch use someone else?

[Buyer: “Yes, then I call around.”]
And when you can’t find it in time, what happens to the order?

[Buyer: “If we can’t find it, the order sits.”]
Is there one part that keeps coming up?

[If they name one.]
Got it. That’s why I called. We can check other sources for [part they named]. Would you be open to ten minutes with our parts specialist to look at that one together?

[If they say “Just email me.”]
Sure. What would you want me to send you?

[If they identify a part and want help with it, make one more ask.]
If it’s [part] you need, would it be easier to look at it together for ten minutes? You could tell us exactly what the replacement needs to fit.

[If they still prefer email.]
Of course. What’s the best email for that? I’ll send you [the item they requested].

[If they accept the meeting, offer two available times.]
Would [day and time] or [second day and time] work better? That’s [time zone].
What’s the best work email for the invite?
Perfect. That’s [confirmed day, time and zone]. We’ll look at [part or order issue].

[Buyer: “Head office decides that.”]
No problem. Who should I speak with about a part the branch can’t source?

[Buyer: “They always cover it. We don’t need a backup.”]
Sounds like you’re covered. Thanks for taking my call.
whyItWorks: A specific part gives the buyer a reason to meet and gives the specialist something to prepare.
personalization: Replace the distributor example with one buyer, one recurring problem and an offer you can deliver.
Use the words the buyer used when you describe the meeting.
Offer two real times only after the buyer has agreed.
If the buyer asks for an email twice, send the specific item you agreed to send.

objections.response: Sure. Is there a part you want me to look at, or did you just want our contact details? If they want the details, send them. If they ask about fit for a particular part, a short working call may be worth offering.
Makes sense. When one of them is out, can the branch go elsewhere, or does everything have to stay with them? If their current suppliers cover it, thank them and move on.
Understood. Is this something you’d want to pick up another day? If yes, agree on a callback time. A callback becomes a meeting only when the buyer agrees to a separate discussion with a purpose.

objections.objection: I’m not the person for that.
objections.response: No problem. Who usually makes the call when a part is holding up an order? Ask whether you may mention the referral before using their name.

alternatives.label: Fill-in appointment setter script
alternatives.description: Swap in your own buyer, offer and meeting purpose.
alternatives.script:
Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Company]. We help [type of business] with [specific task]. Do you look after that?

Curious to ask, how do you handle [situation] today?
[Listen.] And when [gap they mentioned] happens, what does that mean for your team?

Got it. We can help with [their issue]. Would you be open to [short meeting] to [specific purpose]?

[If they hesitate.] What would make that conversation useful for you?
[Ask again only if their answer gives you a reason.] Would [narrower next step] be worth ten minutes?

[If yes.] Does [time] or [time] work better? What’s the best email for the invite? Confirm the day, time, time zone and agenda.

alternatives.description: For a buyer who answers between tasks.
alternatives.script: Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Supplier]. Quick question. Who handles it when your branch needs a part the regular supplier can’t get?

alternatives.label: Voicemail
alternatives.description: Name the job you can help with and leave one clear way back.
alternatives.script: Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Supplier] at [number]. I’m calling about the parts your branch has trouble sourcing. If that lands with you, you can reach me at [number].

faqs.question: What should an appointment setter say at the beginning of a cold call?
faqs.answer: Give your name, the company and one plain reason for calling. Ask whether the person handles that work. Once they confirm, ask how they deal with the situation today.

faqs.question: When should I ask for the meeting?
faqs.answer: Ask after the buyer has described something they would like to solve or compare. Name that issue and what the meeting would accomplish. An interested tone alone gives a salesperson very little to work with.

faqs.question: How do I ask again after “send me an email”?
faqs.answer: Ask what information would help. If the buyer names a genuine issue that is easier to discuss, offer one short conversation about it. If they still want email, honour that choice.

faqs.question: What makes a booked sales meeting qualified?
faqs.answer: For this call, the right person has a real purchasing issue, accepts a specific agenda and agrees to a date and time. Record the words they used and tell the receiving specialist what is still unknown. Track attendance separately.

faqs.question: What should go in the calendar invitation?
faqs.answer: Use the buyer’s words for the agenda, name the people expected to attend and confirm the day, time and time zone. In the parts example, name the item to review so the specialist knows what to bring.

title: IT Staffing Cold Call Script for Hiring Managers
seoTitle: IT Staffing Cold Call Script for Hiring Managers
secondaryKeywords: IT staffing agency cold calling script
cold call to a hiring manager
serviceCategory: IT staffing agencies winning employer clients
objective: Earn a short intake for one open technical contract role
icp: An employer with a verified technical contract opening in a location and skill area the agency can serve.
scenario: An agency rep calls the hiring manager about a posted contract network administrator position.
metaDescription: Copy an IT staffing cold call script for hiring managers. Qualify a contract role, handle preferred agencies and ask for a short job intake before sending résumés.
opening: Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Agency]. I saw the contract network administrator role in [City]. Is that one yours?
quickAnswer: An IT staffing sales call starts with one verified vacancy. Confirm the hiring owner, the work the contractor must handle and whether the employer can use your agency. Earn a job intake before promising a shortlist.
questions: What’s the one thing this person needs to handle on their own in the first week?
When do you need them on site?
Are you open to another recruiting partner for this role?
bridge: Got it. We recruit for that kind of network work. The part I’d want to get right is [requirement they named].
cta: Would you be open to ten minutes with our technical recruiter to go through that before we send anyone over?
fullScript:
[Check the employer’s posting, contract status and location before you dial.]
Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Agency]. I saw the contract network administrator role in [City]. Is that one yours?

[If yes.]
Is it still open?

[If they’re still hiring.]
Curious to ask, what’s the one thing this person needs to handle on their own in the first week?

[Listen. If they name a requirement, follow that thread.]
When you’ve spoken to people so far, what’s been missing?

[If there’s a gap your agency can cover.]
When do you need them on site?
[Pause.] And are you open to another recruiting partner for this role?

[If they can consider your agency.]
Got it. We recruit for that kind of network work. The part I’d want to get right is [requirement they named]. Would you be open to ten minutes with our technical recruiter to go through that before we send anyone over?

[Buyer: “We already have agencies.”]
Makes sense. Are they finding people with [skill they mentioned]?
[If they aren’t.] Can you bring in another agency for this role, or does everything go through the approved list?

[If they say “Just send résumés.”]
Sure. What would rule someone out straight away?

[If they give you a real constraint and outside submissions are allowed, ask again.]
That helps. Would ten minutes with our recruiter be useful to get [specific task] right before we send you a résumé?

[If they accept.]
Would [day and time] or [second day and time] work better? That’s [time zone].
What’s the best work email for the invite?
Perfect. We’ll cover [must-have], [start window] and how you’d like submissions handled.

[If only approved suppliers may submit.]
Understood. Is there a vendor review we can apply for, or is the list closed?
[Buyer: “Talent acquisition handles that.”]
Got it. Who there looks after contract suppliers, and how do they want us to get in touch?

[Buyer: “The list is closed.”]
Understood. I’ll leave it there. Thanks for letting me know.

[Buyer: “We filled it.”]
Good to know. I’ll take it off my list. Thanks for your time.
whyItWorks: The hiring manager can say exactly what a contractor has to do before the recruiter discusses profiles.
personalization: Verify the job on the employer’s own careers page and use its exact title.
Use the person’s answer to choose one technical follow-up you understand.
Confirm the site, start window and approved submission route before promising candidates.
Use the second ask only when the manager names a hiring requirement your recruiter can help with.

objections.response: Makes sense. When they can’t cover a particular skill, can the team consider a specialist, or does every submission have to go through the same list? If the list is closed, thank them. A vendor review date is a follow-up, not a job order.

objections.objection: Talent acquisition owns the agency list.
objections.response: Thanks. Does talent acquisition handle this specific contract too? If they do, who should I ask about the approved route? Stop there if the employer is keeping the search internal.
Good to know. I’ll take it off my list. Don’t try to turn a closed job into a technical intake. Record the change so another caller doesn’t call about the same posting.
Happy to get you the right information. Is there an approved range for this contract, and does it go through procurement? Follow their process. Quote only terms your agency can actually offer.

faqs.question: How do you cold call a hiring manager as an IT recruiter?
faqs.answer: Reference one verified role and ask whether the manager owns it. Confirm it is still open. Ask what the contractor must handle in the first week, then find out whether the employer can consider an outside recruiter.

faqs.question: What if the employer already uses preferred staffing agencies?
faqs.answer: Ask whether those agencies are covering the specific requirement. If there is a gap, confirm whether another supplier can participate. If only approved firms may submit, ask for the formal review route and follow it.

faqs.question: Should I send résumés before a job intake?
faqs.answer: First confirm what the person must do, working conditions, timing and the employer’s submission process. If the manager wants information only, send the agreed material through the authorised route.

faqs.question: What qualifies an IT staffing sales meeting?
faqs.answer: The vacancy is active, the person can discuss the work, the agency can cover the requirement, and there is a permitted way to participate. A meeting has an agreed time and intake purpose. A vendor registration link on its own is a different outcome.

faqs.question: What if a job posting is old or already filled?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the position is still active before discussing recruiting support. If it has closed, update your record and thank the manager. An old posting alone gives you no basis for an intake or a candidate submission.

title: Fleet Account Cold Calling Script for Auto Body Shops
seoTitle: Fleet Account Cold Calling Script for Auto Body Shops
primaryKeyword: fleet account cold calling script for auto body shops
secondaryKeywords: how to get fleet accounts for an auto body shop
collision repair sales script for fleet managers
subindustry: Auto body shops prospecting local service fleets
objective: Find out whether a local fleet can use a second body shop for overflow repairs
icp: Local operators with vans or light trucks your collision shop can repair. Confirm the vehicle mix and where those vehicles are based.
scenario: A local shop wants to introduce its manager to a fleet supervisor who already has a repair supplier.
metaDescription: Use this fleet account cold calling script for auto body shops. Ask who chooses the repair shop, handle “we already have one” and qualify a backup introduction.
opening: When one of your vans needs bodywork, do you choose the shop locally, or does head office handle that?
quickAnswer: A fleet account is worth pursuing when someone can authorise a second estimate. Once you reach that person, ask which vehicles they would send and what would prompt them to call your shop.
questions: Which vehicles would you send to a second shop, and where are they based?
What usually prompts a call to the backup shop?
Who has to approve a new shop before you can request an estimate?
bridge: If you sometimes need a second estimate, our shop manager can check whether those vans fit our bays and tell you who to call.
cta: Would ten minutes with our shop manager help you decide whether to keep us as a backup?
fullScript:
[Introduce yourself.]
Hi [Name], it’s [Rep] at [Shop] in [Town]. When one of your vans needs bodywork, do you choose the shop locally, or does head office handle that?

Fleet manager: “We decide here, but we already have a shop.”
You: “When they’re booked up, can you use a second shop?”

[They can use a backup.]
Fleet manager: “Yes, if ours can’t give us an estimate date.”
You: “Got it. Which vehicles would you send out in that situation?”
Fleet manager: “Mainly service vans. A few are high-roof.”
You: “Where are those vans based?”
Fleet manager: “They all come back to the west depot.”
You: “Does purchasing have to add us before you can request an estimate?”
Fleet manager: “I can ask for a quote. Purchasing approves the shop before we send a van.”

[If the vehicles and location fit.]
You: “Would ten minutes with our shop manager help you decide whether to keep us as a backup?”

[They ask for an email.]
Fleet manager: “Just send me your details.”
You: “Sure. What would help next time you need an estimate?”
Fleet manager: “Your estimate contact and whether you can fit our high-roof vans.”
You: “I’ll check the clearance with our manager. Would it help to speak with them about that model?”
[If they prefer email, confirm the address and send the details. If they want the introduction, offer two times and confirm the time zone and email address before sending the invite.]

[Head office or a fleet management company decides.]
Fleet manager: “All bodywork goes through head office.”
You: “Who at head office handles repair vendors for this depot?”
[Record the route they give you. If the list is closed, thank them and end the call.]

[They can’t use a second shop.]
Fleet manager: “No. Even when ours is full, every van goes through them.”
You: “Got it. Thanks for clearing that up. I’ll leave it there.”
whyItWorks: The first two answers tell you whether the fleet has a choice. A vehicle type, a depot and a reason for the call give the manager something concrete to follow up on.
personalization: Use the name of the shop and the town where it actually repairs vehicles.
Know the vehicle sizes the shop can accept and who can confirm bay clearance.
Use the fleet’s own reason for considering a second estimate.
Confirm any pickup, estimate timing or onboarding details with the shop before promising them.

objections.response: “If your usual shop can’t give you an estimate date, who can approve another quote?” If purchasing makes that decision, ask how a shop can get on its list.
“Who looks after approved body shops for this depot?” Record the contact or application process the supervisor gives you.

objections.objection: Can you pick up a high-roof van and have it back Friday?
objections.response: “Which model is it, and where is it parked? I’ll check with the shop manager and get you an answer.” Agree who will call back. Pickup, bay clearance and repair timing all need confirmation.
“Of course. Do you just want our estimate contact, or is there a specific van you need us to check?” If the contact is all they want, send it and finish.

faqs.question: What should a body shop say when calling fleet managers?
faqs.answer: Give your name, your shop and your town. Ask who chooses the repairer when a van needs bodywork, then pause. The answer tells you whether to speak with the depot manager or ask for the head-office contact.

faqs.question: How do I get fleet repair accounts if the fleet already has a body shop?
faqs.answer: Look for a specific gap you can cover. A depot might need an estimate for a high-roof van while its regular shop is full. Confirm the depot can send that work elsewhere and your shop can take the model.

faqs.question: What belongs in the handoff to the shop manager?
faqs.answer: Record the depot, vehicle type, who approves a second shop, when the fleet would use it, and what the manager needs to confirm. Include the agreed next step and time zone. Mark a repair order only after the fleet actually authorizes work.

faqs.question: What if the driver or depot manager cannot choose the repair shop?
faqs.answer: Ask who maintains the approved vendor list. That might be head office or the fleet management company. If they give you a route, record it. If they have no route for a new shop, close the call.

faqs.question: Can CallTeam call fleet managers for a collision repair shop?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give CallTeam your service radius, the vehicles your bays can take and the name of your estimate contact. CallTeam uses those details to qualify fleet managers for an introduction. Your shop confirms capacity and handles estimates.

title: Commercial Real Estate Cold Calling Script for Property Owners
seoTitle: Commercial Real Estate Cold Calling Script for Owners
primaryKeyword: commercial real estate cold calling script
secondaryKeywords: industrial real estate broker cold call
calling an owner who is holding
subindustry: Industrial property owners and asset managers
objective: Confirm who decides on a commercial property and earn permission for one relevant follow-up
icp: Owners and authorised asset managers whose commercial buildings fit the brokerage’s market and property type.
scenario: An industrial broker has checked an ownership record. The person who answers is keeping the building, but may find a verified sale useful.
metaDescription: Use this commercial real estate cold calling script to reach property owners, handle “we’re holding” and offer one verified comparable. Copy the broker’s call notes.
opening: Hi [Name], it’s [Rep] with [Brokerage]. Do you still look after [Property] on [Street]?
quickAnswer: Identify the property and find out who makes decisions about it. A broker earns a follow-up by tying a documented sale to something the owner is working on, such as a lease renewal or a discussion with a partner.
questions: Who makes the ownership decisions for this building?
What are your plans for this building over the next year?
Which difference would matter most if I sent you a sale to look at?
bridge: I can send the sale I checked, where I found it and the one difference you mentioned.
cta: Would it help to compare a nearby sale before you and your partner decide? I can walk you through it in ten minutes.
fullScript:
[Before dialling, check the property address, the ownership record and the source of any sale you plan to mention.]
Hi [Name], it’s [Rep] with [Brokerage]. Do you still look after [Property] on [Street]?

Owner: “Yes. Why?”
You: “I work with industrial owners in [Area]. What are you thinking of doing with the building over the next year?”

[They are holding.]
Owner: “We’re holding it.”
You: “Understood. Would a sale nearby be useful for your planning, or are you all set?”
Owner: “We’d look at one. Ours has two tenants, though.”
You: “I can send the price and floor area. I haven’t confirmed the lease terms. Would those figures still help?”
Owner: “Yes. Email it to me.”
You: “What’s the best work email? I’ll put the address and source in the note.”
[Send the one item promised. Log email only unless the owner agrees to a call.]

[A lease decision is coming up.]
Owner: “My partner and I might sell once a lease comes up.”
You: “When are you two reviewing it?”
Owner: “Early next month.”
You: “What would help you decide?”
Owner: “I’d like to know if anyone’s buying buildings our size when a lease is about to expire.”
You: “Would it help to compare a nearby sale before you and your partner decide? I can walk you through it in ten minutes.”
[If yes, offer two times. Confirm who will join, their work email and the time zone. If the sale doesn’t answer the lease question, say so.]

[They already have a broker.]
Owner: “Our broker handles that for us.”
You: “Got it. Does your broker already bring you the sales you need?”
[If yes, thank them and close. If the owner requests one source, confirm how they would like to receive it.]

[You reached the property manager.]
Manager: “I look after the tenants. Ownership handles sales.”
You: “Thanks. Who should I speak with about the owner’s plans for [Property]?”
[If there is no referral, end here.]

[No fit.]
Owner: “We’re keeping it and we don’t want updates.”
You: “Understood. I’ll leave it there. Thanks for your time.”
whyItWorks: A street address gives the owner a quick way to correct the caller. Asking what the owner would use makes the next step specific, including when that next step is a single email.
personalization: Check the building address, ownership entity and authorised contact before calling.
Pick a closed transaction in the same asset class and area. Record the source and sale date.
Ask which differences matter to this owner before treating the buildings as comparable.
Send only the agreed material and record whether the owner requested a follow-up call.

objections.response: “Is there anything you’re keeping an eye on while you hold it?” If nothing comes to mind, thank the owner and finish the call.
“Does your broker already bring you what you need?” If the relationship covers it, thank the owner. If they ask for a particular public sale, send only what they requested.
“Who handles ownership decisions for this building?” Ask for the business contact if they can share it. A manager overseeing tenants might have no role in selling the property.

objections.objection: Do you actually have a buyer?
objections.response: If you are calling about market information, say so. “I’m calling about a recorded sale. I don’t have a buyer to bring you for this building.” Let the owner decide whether the information is still useful.
“Sure. What would you like me to send?” If the owner asks for the price, send the sale record with the address and date. Arrange a call only if there’s a question they want to discuss.

alternatives.label: Fill-in call for a commercial building owner
alternatives.description: Use one verified building and a reason for that owner to stay on the line.
alternatives.script:
[Name], this is [Rep] at [Brokerage]. Who reviews offers on [Address]?

[If they decide] I cover [property type] in [area]. Are you keeping the building for the time being?

[If there is a decision ahead] What information would help? I checked [closed sale] in [source] on [date]. Would you like the details, or would a short call about [specific difference] be useful?

alternatives.label: Opener when you reach an asset manager
alternatives.description: Separate ownership decisions from day-to-day building management.
alternatives.script: Hi [Name], [Rep] with [Brokerage]. I’m calling about [Address]. When the ownership group reviews whether to hold or sell that building, is that something you handle?

alternatives.label: Voicemail for a commercial property owner
alternatives.description: Use this only when you have checked the sale you mention.
alternatives.script: Hi [Name], it’s [Rep] with [Brokerage], calling about [Address]. I have the recorded details of an industrial sale in [area]. If that would help with your planning, I’m at [number]. Again, it’s [Rep] at [number].

faqs.question: What should a commercial real estate broker say when cold calling property owners?
faqs.answer: Give your name and brokerage, name the property, then confirm you have the person who looks after it. Ask about the owner’s plans before offering market information or a meeting.

faqs.question: What do I say if the owner says they are holding the property?
faqs.answer: Ask whether a sale would help with a lease review, refinancing or a conversation with a partner. If the owner requests an email, confirm the address and send the one record they asked for.

faqs.question: What makes a comparable sale useful on a broker prospecting call?
faqs.answer: Start with a confirmed closed sale. Record its source, date, building type, location and size. Ask about the differences that matter to the owner, such as tenancy or loading. Flag missing terms before anyone draws a conclusion about value.

faqs.question: How do I handle an owner who already has representation?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the owner’s broker already provides the information they use. If yes, close courteously. If they request a particular record, respect the route they specify.

faqs.question: Can CallTeam call commercial property owners for a brokerage?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give CallTeam the property types, neighbourhoods and ownership criteria you want to cover. CallTeam qualifies the owner’s reason to meet and books the call. The brokerage verifies comparables and handles valuation and listing advice.
